questions.q: If the lines represented by the equations a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 are coincident, then the correct relation is
sol: Coincident lines are the same line, so all three ratios are equal: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂.

sol: All equilateral triangles have every angle 60° and all sides in the same ratio, so any two are similar.

questions.q: Write the degree of a linear polynomial.
sol: A linear polynomial has the form ax + b (a ≠ 0), so its degree is 1.

questions.q: Write the formula to find the total surface area of a cube of edge ‘a’ units.
sol: A cube has 6 equal square faces, each of area a². TSA = 6a².

questions.q:
In the given frequency distribution table, write the modal class:
Class-interval: 1–3, 3–5, 5–7, 7–9
Frequency: 4, 8, 2, 2
sol: The modal class is the class with the highest frequency. The highest frequency is 8, for 3 – 5.

questions.q: Write the probability of an impossible event.
sol: An impossible event never happens, so its probability is 0.

questions.q: How many solutions do the pair of linear equations 2x + 3y − 9 = 0 and 3x + 2y − 6 = 0 have?
sol: Since a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂, the lines intersect at one point, so there is exactly one solution.

questions.q: Write the zeroes of the polynomial y = p(x) in the given graph.
questions.fig: Graph of an upward-opening parabola y = p(x) that cuts the x-axis at x = −1 and x = 4 (and the y-axis at −4).
sol: The zeroes are the x-coordinates where the graph meets the x-axis: −1 and 4.

questions.q: Write the roots of the quadratic equation x(x + 2) = 0.
sol: x = 0 or x + 2 = 0, so x = 0 or x = −2.

questions.q: In the given figure, write the similarity criterion used to show that ΔABC ~ ΔQRP.
questions.fig: ΔABC with AB = 2, AC = 3, BC = 2.5. ΔQRP with QR = 4, QP = 6, RP = 5.
sol: All three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so the criterion is SSS.

questions.q: In the given figure, ∠ABC = 90°. Write the values of the following: (i) sin α (ii) tan θ
questions.fig: Right triangle ABC, right-angled at B. AB = 3 units, BC = 4 units, AC = 5 units. θ is the angle at A and α is the angle at C.
sol: For α (at C): opposite side = AB = 3, hypotenuse = AC = 5, so sin α = 3/5.
For θ (at A): opposite side = BC = 4, adjacent side = AB = 3, so tan θ = 4/3.

questions.q: Prove that 6 + √2 is an irrational number.
sol: Assume 6 + √2 is rational. Then 6 + √2 = a/b, where a, b are integers and b ≠ 0.
a and b are integers, so (a − 6b)/b is rational. That would make √2 rational.
But √2 is irrational. This contradiction shows our assumption is wrong.

or.q: The HCF and LCM of two positive integers are respectively 4 and 60. If one of the integers is 20, then find the other integer.
sol: HCF × LCM = product of the two numbers.

questions.q:
Solve the given pair of linear equations by elimination method:
2x + y = 10
x − y = 2
sol: Add the two equations: 3x = 12, so x = 4.
Substitute in x − y = 2: 4 − y = 2, so y = 2.

sol: D < 0, so the equation has no real roots.

questions.q: According to Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, if 40 = xʸ · z, then find the values of x, y and z.
sol: Comparing with xʸ · z: x = 2, y = 3, z = 5.

questions.q: If A(1, y), B(4, 3), C(x, 6) and D(3, 5) are the vertices of a parallelogram taken in an order, then find the values of x and y.
sol: Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so the mid-point of AC = mid-point of BD.

questions.q: Find the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial p(x) = x² + 7x + 10 and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
Prove that “The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact”.
sol: Given: a circle with centre O and a tangent XY at point P. To prove: OP ⟂ XY.
Take any point Q on XY other than P and join OQ.
Q lies outside the circle (a tangent touches the circle only at P), so OQ > OP (radius).
This is true for every point Q on XY other than P, so OP is the shortest distance from O to XY.
The shortest segment from a point to a line is the perpendicular, so OP ⟂ XY.

questions.q: Prove that: cos A/(1 + sin A) + (1 + sin A)/cos A = 2 sec A.
sol: LHS = [cos²A + (1 + sin A)²] / [(1 + sin A) cos A]
= [cos²A + 1 + 2 sin A + sin²A] / [(1 + sin A) cos A]
= [2 + 2 sin A] / [(1 + sin A) cos A]   (since sin²A + cos²A = 1)
= 2(1 + sin A) / [(1 + sin A) cos A] = 2/cos A = 2 sec A = RHS.

questions.q: A box contains 20 cards numbered from 1 to 20. One card is drawn randomly from the box. Find the probability of getting a card bearing (i) a perfect square number (ii) a number which is divisible by both 2 and 3.
sol: (ii) Divisible by both 2 and 3 means divisible by 6: 6, 12, 18 → 3 outcomes. P = 3/20.

questions.q: The difference between the altitude and base of a right angled triangle is 5 cm. If the area of the triangle is 150 cm², then find the base and altitude of the triangle.
sol: Let base = x cm, so altitude = (x + 5) cm.

or.q: The sum of the squares of two consecutive even positive integers is 164. Find the integers.
sol: Let the integers be x and x + 2.

questions.q: Two line segments AB and CD intersect each other at a point ‘O’. Join AC and BD such that AC ∥ BD and prove that ΔAOC ~ ΔBOD.
sol: ∠OAC = ∠OBD (alternate angles, since AC ∥ BD and AB is a transversal).
So ΔAOC ~ ΔBOD by the AA similarity criterion.

sol: Plot both lines on graph paper. They intersect at (2, 3).

questions.q: Prove that “If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio”.
sol: Given: In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC, with D on AB and E on AC. To prove: AD/DB = AE/EC.
Construction: Join BE and CD. Draw EN ⟂ AB and DM ⟂ AC.
ar(ADE)/ar(BDE) = (½ × AD × EN)/(½ × DB × EN) = AD/DB.
ar(ADE)/ar(DEC) = (½ × AE × DM)/(½ × EC × DM) = AE/EC.
ΔBDE and ΔDEC are on the same base DE and between the same parallels DE and BC, so ar(BDE) = ar(DEC).

questions.q: A solid consisting of a right circular cone of height 120 cm and radius 60 cm standing on a hemisphere of radius 60 cm is placed upright in a right circular cylinder full of water such that it touches the bottom as shown in the figure. If the radius of the cylinder is 60 cm and height is 180 cm, then find the volume of water left in the cylinder in terms of π.
questions.fig: A cylinder of radius 60 cm, height 180 cm, full of water. Inside it stands a solid: a hemisphere (radius 60 cm) at the bottom with a cone (height 120 cm) on top.
sol: Volume of cylinder = πr²h = π × 60² × 180 = 648000π cm³.

or.q: A solid is made of a cylinder with a hemispherical depression having the same radius (‘r’ cm) as that of cylinder at the top end as shown in the figure. The volume of the hemispherical depression is 18000π cm³. If the height of the cylinder is 145 cm, then find the total surface area of the solid.
or.fig: A solid cylinder (height 145 cm) with a hemisphere of the same radius scooped out of its top face.
sol: Inner surface of the hemispherical depression = 2πr² = 1800π (it replaces the flat top).

questions.q: An arithmetic progression consists of 16 terms. The sum of all its terms is 768. If the last term of the progression is 93, then find the arithmetic progression. Also show that the sum of all the terms of this progression is equal to 3 times the sum of first 16 odd natural numbers using formula.
sol: 3 × 256 = 768, which equals the sum of the AP. Shown.

questions.q: A pole and a tower are standing vertically on a level ground. The height of the pole is 6 m and the angle of elevation to the top of the pole from the bottom of the tower is 30°. The angle of elevation to the top of the tower from the top of the pole is 60° as shown in the figure. Find the height of the tower (CD). Also find the distance (AC) between the top of the pole and the top of the tower.
questions.fig: Pole AB (A at the top, B at the foot) and tower CD (C at the top, D at the foot) on level ground. Angle of elevation of A from D is 30°; angle of elevation of C from A is 60°.
sol: In ΔABD: tan 30° = AB/BD, so 1/√3 = 6/BD and BD = 6√3 m.
Draw AE ⟂ CD. Then AE = BD = 6√3 m and ED = AB = 6 m.
In ΔAEC: tan 60° = CE/AE, so CE = √3 × 6√3 = 18 m.
